artifact: Urdu sentence bank editorial audit summary

critical_examples.issue: Urdu plural subject paired with singular English, plus target spelling error.
Target says بڑی (big) where the English requires بری (bad) at sports.
Target says bitter while English says sour.
Target asks whether everything was done correctly; English asks whether anything has ever been done right.
Target says speaker is already lying in bed; English says speaker has to go to bed.
Malformed present Urdu is paired with a past English statement plus tag question.
Target says sometimes; English says almost never.
Target says bad; English says big.
Target says death sentence; English says life sentence.
Target is future; English is past.
Target says diamond necklace; English says pearl necklace.
Target refers to cotton and does not match English crops are much better.
Target uses export; English requires import.
Target says under sixteen; English says sixteen or younger.

root_cause: The current sentence builder filters licensing, script plausibility, target uniqueness, and length, then ranks primarily from English-side usefulness. It does not validate target-language grammar, spelling, idiomaticity, register, or bilingual semantic equivalence before selecting the top 1000.
release_requirements: Convert all confirmed findings into a source-locked curated correction/replacement layer.
Keep uncertain/native-judgment rows out of automatic promotion until independently reviewed.
Regenerate Urdu sentence CSV and all sentence-bearing PDFs from the curated layer together.
Run deterministic regression checks against the audited source hash and corrected learner pairs.
Complete an independent native/editorial review before any absolute correctness claim.
